new_discrepancies.description: Two statements are stronger than the old library supports. Item 1 says every old theorem with a hypothesis `he : N.IsTrajOn ...` is silent about disturbed trajectories; item 2 says the disturbance cannot be hidden in the netlist and that a current source satisfies neither time-independence nor passivity. In fact a bounded disturbance can be written as an ordinary old-style device (a time-independent function of its terminal voltages, driven from a boundary node), and one old theorem, IsInvCore.propagation_side, then applies to exactly the disturbed trajectories of Appendix A. What is lost is passivity, hence rail invariance, and the IsInverter theorems (which forbid any other channel at the output). The audit's own §11.1 row 7 and pitfall A1 rely on propagation_side covering 'an extra bounded inflow', which is at odds with the universal wording here. The main conclusions of §6 are unaffected: rail invariance still fails and propagation_side still assumes the rail.
